messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Merged HMC Refactor
parts:
I merged the hmc_refactor branch into master -- there weren't any conflicts outside of stan/src/mcmc. Once I have a second (maybe on the plane, if I don't fall asleep?) I'll add the epsilon jitter to both NUTS and static HMC. Until then, please let me know if the merge broke anyone's models! Or if there are any particular performances changes.

Next step -- a unified mcmc_writer class to handle both sample and diagnostic output (Dan, if you have any downtime between that dissonant young-persons music let me know what changes you made in the visual_diagnostic branch to admit unconstrained variable names) and revamped command-line options (I think we agreed upon sub arguments -- is this possible with the current argument parser, or do we need to rewrite that first?).

-Mike

P.S. Peter, you should be able to add all kinds of Metropolis fun in stan/src/mcmc/metro and use the base adaptation classes for adaptive Metropolis algorithms, too. As I noted above, we'll have to revamp the command line arguments anyways, so go ahead and add whatever arguments you'd like to get Metropolis running.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Merged HMC Refactor; fvar<int>
parts:
You want to do it for all types T,
but you still want to return what
numeric_limits<double> returns.

All the types T you'll implement it for
will have implicit constructors T(double)
that will build the appropriate type out
of doubles.

At the very least, we'll need the following
for RM-HMC in Stan:

fvar<double>
fvar<var>
fvar<fvar<double>>
fvar<fvar<var>>

But they can all be implemented with one template.
And templating will also let client code plug in
float instead of double or some other base scalar
type.

- Bob
